candidates.label: Galilee (historical region)
candidates.support: Wikidata's current representative point for the Galilee region sits roughly 30 km north of the point OpenBible.info recorded for the same Wikidata item in its own snapshot; both are reasonable approximations for a large, imprecisely bounded historical region rather than a single site, and both fall within the broad area described as Galilee in first-century sources.

summary.text: Galilee was the hill country and lakeside region of northern Israel in the first century AD, home to Nazareth, Capernaum and the other towns beside the Sea of Galilee where most of Jesus' public ministry, as narrated in the Gospels, is set.

history.text: Roman-era Galilee was administratively distinct from Judea for most of the first century, governed first by a Herodian tetrarch and only folded into direct Roman provincial rule alongside Judea after AD 44.

otConnections.note: Isaiah's oracle naming 'Galilee of the nations' is quoted in Matthew 4:15-16 as finding fulfillment when Jesus based his ministry in Galilee.
